text:
morgan: Thinking out loud — proposal to move toward thin adapter layers between runtime and business services to simplify migrations and pay down coupling debt. Sketch: small gRPC/HTTP shims that implement a stable ‘provider’ contract and translate to internal shapes. low-risk incremental rollout. :thinking_face:
 alex: short version — adapters = small translation layer per service, right? how do we avoid doubling serialization cost for hot paths?
 morgan: yes. hot-paths keep fast path with co-located adapter and optimized codec (same process), adapter becomes a shim only when we need to swap or split ownership. goal is to enable bounded extraction without big cutovers.
 kai: sounds promising. tradeoffs: more moving parts, more tests. do we have enough infra to manage extra deploy units?
 sasha: +1 on tests. also need a clear contract format. propose a simple proto with version and stable enum for routing keys.
 morgan: agreed. propose contract fields: version, model_profile_id, sequence_hint, client_latency_budget. keep it intentionally tiny.
 niraj: curious about stateful components — where does session ownership live? if adapter sits between runtime and session store we'll need session shims too.
 morgan: session still owned by session service. adapter will forward session ids and provide optional local cache for reads to avoid roundtrips. caching policy configurable per adapter.
 alex: can we get an example of the adapter interface? pseudocode would help.
 morgan: sure —
 morgan: ```
 service ProviderAdapter {
   rpc HandleRequest(ProviderRequest) returns (ProviderResponse);
 }
 message ProviderRequest { string version = 1; string session_id = 2; bytes payload = 3; int32 seq_len = 4; }
 ```
 kai: looks clean. what about error semantics? connecting failures must bubble with codes so router can fallback to hosted model.
 sasha: add transient vs permanent error field and a suggested fallback hint. also log correlation id for traceability.
 niraj: ops question — how will we roll this out? canary per region? traffic split?
 morgan: rollout plan: 1) build local adapter variant with feature flag, 2) deploy to non-prod and run traffic mirror, 3) canary 5% in us-west, monitor tokens/sec and p99 latency for 48h, 4) increase if stable. auto-failback on error rate spike >= 0.5%.
 alex: metrics to watch: adapter_cpu, adapter_latency_p99, token_retention_rate, error_mode_counts. add an SLO dashboard tile.
 sasha: what about tech debt accounting? each adapter should have a debt tag and a planned removal ETA if it's a shim to support legacy surface.
 morgan: yes — require a DebtCard in the PR with owner, risk, and sunset date.
 deploy-bot: deploy preview created for branch morgan/thin-adapters — preview-url: https://ci.redwood.internal/preview/2312 :rocket:
 niraj: can someone write a short RFC with acceptance criteria? want: interface proto, rollout plan, tests, debt tagging, performance regression checklist.
 alex: I can draft the RFC tomorrow. will ping for review.
 sasha: I'll handle the contract proto and initial test harness.
 kai: I'll look at infra needs for deploy units and add a cost estimate.
 morgan: awesome — thanks. next sync: friday 11am to review RFC draft. :thumbsup:
